questions.q: Why doesn't a flow immediately see individual fields like 'status' after an HTTP action calls Meridian TrackAPI?
options: Power Automate automatically parses every API response
The response body is treated as a single string until something tells the flow its structure
Meridian TrackAPI doesn't return any data
Fields are only available after the flow finishes running
questions.explain: An HTTP response is just text to Power Automate. Parse JSON is what turns that text into typed, clickable dynamic content field by field.

questions.q: What does a Parse JSON schema describe?
options: The visual layout of the flow in the designer
The structure — field names and types — that Parse JSON uses to interpret incoming JSON text
The order in which actions run
The authentication method used by the HTTP action
questions.explain: The schema tells Parse JSON what fields to expect and what type each one is, which is how it turns raw text into dynamic content.

questions.q: What is the recommended way to build a Parse JSON schema?
options: Write the schema from scratch using a JSON reference guide
Use 'Use sample payload to generate schema' with a real example response
Copy the schema from a completely unrelated flow
Skip the schema and reference the raw string directly
questions.explain: Pasting in one real sample payload and letting Power Automate generate the schema automatically is the standard approach, and it matches field names and types accurately.

questions.q: How is the Compose action different from Parse JSON?
options: Compose requires a schema just like Parse JSON
Compose evaluates and holds the result of one expression, without parsing a JSON structure into fields
Compose can only be used with SharePoint connectors
Compose and Parse JSON are two names for the same action
questions.explain: Compose is a general-purpose scratchpad for one expression's result — useful for debugging or reuse — while Parse JSON specifically turns a JSON string into schema-defined fields.

questions.q: A Castlebridge flow's Parse JSON action starts throwing an error after Meridian changes its API. What most likely happened?
options: The flow simply needs to be re-saved
A field the existing schema depends on changed or disappeared from Meridian's response
Compose actions always expire after 30 days
Parse JSON stopped working permanently and must be replaced
questions.explain: Parse JSON throws a schema-mismatch error when the incoming JSON no longer matches the expected schema — commonly because the source API changed a field the schema relies on.
